Current understanding of taurine’s dose-response relationship remains unclear due to conflicting evidence across studies. While low-dose acute supplementation (1 g) showed no performance benefits in cycling time trials (13), chronic high-dose administration (6 g/day) improved maximal oxygen uptake (7) but required prolonged use (14). Animal studies suggest moderate doses (3–4 g) may offer acute thermoregulatory advantages, though human data under controlled environmental stress remain limited (6, 10, 15).
